subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should public `cron run` be a permanently non-consuming operator/debug action, with only internal timer and gateway watcher paths allowed to consume one-shot scheduler state?
rationale: This is a deliberate compatibility change to the meaning of an existing public cron operation; source-level correctness cannot decide whether preserving historical manual consumption is required for existing operators.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming manual runs
options.body: Keep the proposed internal origin boundary, document that public manual runs preserve scheduler state, and require final-head live proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve legacy consumption
options.body: Keep manual `cron run` consuming one-shots and pursue a separate explicit preview or dry-run workflow instead.

options.title: Add an explicit opt-in consume path
options.body: Make default manual runs non-consuming but define a reviewed public override only if operators need intentional one-shot consumption.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming manual runs
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed internal origin boundary, document that public manual runs preserve scheduler state, and require final-head live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the adjacent gateway on-exit delete-after-run contract that this decision must preserve.
